overview: Two ways a genotype can fail to translate into a perfectly predictable phenotype.
genZNote: Penetrance: does the trait show up at all? Expressivity: if it shows up, how loud is it?

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: The percentage of individuals with a given genotype who actually show the expected phenotype.
aspects.valueB: The degree or intensity to which a trait is expressed in individuals who do show it.

aspects.label: Measured As
aspects.valueB: A range or severity scale within affected individuals.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: BRCA1 mutation carriers who never develop breast cancer show incomplete penetrance.
aspects.valueB: Polydactyly can range from a small extra digit stub to a fully formed extra finger — variable expressivity.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Incomplete penetrance explains why a dominant disease allele can 'skip' an apparently unaffected carrier.
overlay.memoryTrick: Penetrance = whether it shows. Expressivity = how much it shows.
overlay.commonMisconception: Incomplete penetrance is not the same as recessive inheritance — the allele is still dominant, it just doesn't always show up.
